notes: Correct core fix through Dispenser and Token helpers, though the Dispenser bounds check duplicates what Token() already does; it misses the quoted-'{}' and HasSuffix refinements but has good subtests, unbalanced-brace error tests and a realistic adapt test.

Correct and complete for brace nesting, but it adds a redundant layer of Dispenser wrappers with duplicated bounds checks (Token() already guards range) and leaves the `{}` and address HasSuffix quoted cases untouched; tests are good, including unbalanced-error cases and an integration test.

Adds unquoted-brace helpers on Token and Dispenser and applies them in all the structural places, matching the core reference fix, but leaves the quoted '{}' branch and the address HasSuffix check unchanged, and its tests cover only happy paths with no error cases.

Correct core fix with Token plus Dispenser helpers, but it skips the `{}` and quoted-address refinements; its tests cover positive parse and dispenser cases only, with no error cases and no integration test.

Closely mirrors the reference, including skipping the address HasSuffix check for quoted tokens (only the quoted-'{}' branch is left alone), and adds solid dispenser, parser (with error cases) and adapt tests.

Clean Token-method approach that mirrors the reference closely, including the quoted-address HasSuffix fix, though it leaves the `{}` branch matching quoted text; tests cover nesting after a quoted brace, unbalanced errors, and an adapt integration case.

Clean Token helpers including isEmptyBlock, which matches the reference's quoted-'{}' handling (only the address HasSuffix tweak is missing); very thorough tests cover double quotes, backticks, heredocs, nesting, snippets, unbalanced-error cases and an adapt test.

Consistently replaces every structural brace check with clean Token helpers, and also makes the `{}` check quoting-aware as the reference does; it misses only the quoted-address HasSuffix tweak, and its tests are thorough (double quotes, backticks, heredocs, snippets, nesting, error cases, integration).

Clean slice-based fix with a useful slices.Clip aliasing guard and solid table tests (for_each, count, mixed, in-module), but the parent override is still applied to the whole config resource rather than per instance, so module-override cases still silently drop imports.

Returning a flat slice fixes the reported single-module for_each/count case and matches the reference signature, and the slices.Clip aliasing fix is a sensible extra, but parent-over-child override still works per ConfigResource rather than per instance, so a child's import of a different instance is still silently dropped (hidden tests 1/3).

Returning a slice fixes the reported root-module case, but parent/child overrides are still deduplicated per ConfigResource rather than per instance, so child imports for other instances (or other module instances) are still silently dropped; one test case even locks in that dropping.

A clean slice-plus-owner-map approach fixes the single-module case, but its 'parent module overrides child' test explicitly asserts that the child's import of a different instance becomes a Create, which enshrines the same silent-drop failure the issue complains about.

Has the same coarse ConfigResource-level cross-module override flaw as the others, plus a large unrequested refactor (a per-instance expandedImport type and an O(n^2) regrouping in transform_config) that touches many signatures without fixing the instance-level override.

It fixes the reported case and also threads per-instance import config through node_resource_plan, but it adds broad signature churn and an O(n²) grouping in transform_config that the task did not need, while keeping the ConfigResource-level cross-module drop that fails the instance-level hidden tests.

A map-of-slices restructuring fixes the root-module repro and adds a unit test with fixtures, but it is more convoluted than needed and keeps the same config-level cross-module dedup that drops child imports targeting other instances.

A map of slices keeps all same-module blocks and fixes the reported case, but it is more convoluted than a plain slice and keeps the coarse ConfigResource-level cross-module override that still drops child blocks for other instances; it adds a reasonable unit test with fixture plus a plan test.
